section_summary.extract_value: This section presents findings from a single study examining the relationship between body dissatisfaction and positive body image (body appreciation and body image flexibility) in a multi-ethnic college female sample, with particular focus on Black young women. The study used an affect regulation framework and found that BMI was the most significant negative predictor of positive body image, while the discrepancy between current and personal ideal body size was the most consistent body dissatisfaction contributor; notably, BMI did not moderate the relationship between body dissatisfaction and positive body image, yet heavier Black adolescent females reported higher body dissatisfaction and lower body appreciation and flexibility.
